front.title: Interval Absence Claims in Agent Auditing: Problem Statement, Requirements, and Test Scenarios

abstract.t:
Audit records for software agents are designed to show what an agent did. Relying parties also ask a different question: whether an agent could have used a capability at any time during a stated interval. Records of actions cannot answer that question, because authority that goes unused leaves no record of use, even if it existed for part of the interval.
This document describes the problem of interval absence claims, defines terms, lists requirements that an audit evidence system needs to meet before it can support such claims, and gives test scenarios that expose false claims of absence. It does not define a protocol, a data format, or a verification algorithm. It is intended as input to discussions of auditing for agent delegation and interactions.
